newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stock index ends higher, avoid Dow selloff.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stock index ends higher, avoid Dow selloff.

text.p: The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 index ended higher on Monday as surging oil stocks propped up the Canadian market during a selloff on Wall Street.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 5.67 points to close at 5712.55 on volume of 85.1 million shares worth C$1.4 billion ($1.02 billion).
But the overall market finished mixed. Declining stocks outnumbered advances 536 to 425 with 293 issues unchanged.
"Most of the major oil stocks are up and that is pretty well the strength of the TSE," said Rolie Bradley, an institutional salesman with Maison Placements Canada Inc.
The TSE's oil and gas group added 147 points as crude oil futures climbed on a cold weather lead rally.
February Brent jumped more than US$1.00 a barrel after forecasts for a lengthy period of cold weather in some U.S. regions drove NYMEX heating oil prices higher.
The energy group -- which led gains in six of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors -- was followed by gold and forestry products.
The weak side was led by financial services, communications, utilities and consumer products. The Dow Jones Average sank 36 points amid a wave of profit taking in the technology sector.
* Among buoyant oils, Renaissance Energy Ltd. jumped 1.55 to 45 on 463,000 shares. Imperial Oil Ltd. improved 1.45 to 60.05 on 78,000 shares, while Talisman Energy Inc. rose 1.45 to 43.45.
* Barrick Gold Corp. gained 1.45 to 40.25 after it and Bre-X Minerals Ltd. said they have reached a deal to develop the rich Busang gold find in Indonesia.
Bre-X sank 0.90 to 20.10 on 4.8 million shares, the TSE's top issue by volume.
* Placer Dome Inc. fell 0.05 to close at 30.80 after dropping its takeover bid for Australia's Highlands Gold Ltd.
